title: The Cat That Wasn't Dead
complaintTemplate: CUST STATES: check-engine light came on, shop pulled P0420 and quoted $1,400 for a catalytic converter. Car runs fine, no noise, mileage seems normal. Customer wants a second opinion before buying a converter.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Cheap fix. A hairline crack in the flex pipe just ahead of the rear O2 bung lets exhaust pulses draw outside air in; the rear sensor sees that oxygen and reports a converter that isn't storing any. Converter is fine. Correct fix: repair the exhaust leak. Confirming test: act_exhaust_smoke.

activeFaults.label: cracked flex pipe drawing air in ahead of the rear O2 sensor

resultOverrides.act_scope_o2: The upstream sensor switches normally. The downstream sensor wanders and drifts lean instead of holding steady — but it does move when you force the mixture rich.
resultOverrides.act_exhaust_smoke: With the tailpipe blocked and the system filled with smoke, smoke seeps steadily from a hairline crack in the flex pipe just ahead of the rear O2 sensor bung.
resultOverrides.act_fuel_trims: Short and long-term trims are within a few percent at idle and cruise. No misfire counts on any cylinder.
resultOverrides.act_backpressure: Backpressure is within spec — nothing is restricted.
resultOverrides.act_clear_drive: The code clears, then P0420 sets again after a couple of drive cycles.

faultSeeds.internalNote: The sensor lying about the converter. The downstream O2 sensor is lazy/skewed — it sits at a fixed bias and won't respond to a forced mixture change, so the monitor fails a converter that's actually fine. Correct fix: downstream O2 sensor. Confirming test: act_scope_o2 (specifically that it does NOT respond to a forced rich/lean).

activeFaults.label: lazy downstream O2 sensor that won't respond to a forced mixture change

resultOverrides.act_scope_o2: The upstream sensor switches normally. The downstream sensor sits nearly flat at a fixed bias and doesn't move at all when you force the mixture rich, then lean.
resultOverrides.act_exhaust_smoke: The smoke test shows no leaks anywhere ahead of the rear sensor.
resultOverrides.act_fuel_trims: Trims are within a few percent. No misfire counts stored or accumulating.
resultOverrides.act_clear_drive: The code clears and returns after a couple of drive cycles.

faultSeeds.internalNote: COMPOUND — the expensive answer is right, but only halfway. The converter genuinely is dead (rear sensor mirrors the front), AND a chronic cylinder-3 misfire is what cooked it. Replacing the converter alone is a comeback: the misfire kills the new one. Correct fix: repair the misfire AND replace the converter. Confirming tests: act_scope_o2 (dead converter) + act_fuel_trims (the misfire that caused it).

activeFaults.label: catalytic converter no longer storing oxygen
chronic cylinder-3 misfire that cooked the converter

resultOverrides.act_scope_o2: The upstream sensor switches normally and the downstream sensor mirrors it almost move for move — it is tracking the front sensor instead of staying steady. It does respond to a forced mixture change.
resultOverrides.act_exhaust_smoke: No leaks found anywhere ahead of the rear sensor.
resultOverrides.act_fuel_trims: Cylinder 3 is accumulating misfire counts under load, with a stored history misfire code for that cylinder. The other five stay at zero.
resultOverrides.act_backpressure: Backpressure is slightly elevated but still inside spec.
resultOverrides.act_clear_drive: The code clears and comes back quickly.

nodes.prompt: P0420, a $1,400 converter quote, and a car that drives fine. Before you sell that converter — or talk them out of it — where do you start?

options.label: Graph both O2 sensors and see what the rear one is actually reporting
Smoke-test the exhaust for leaks ahead of the rear sensor
Pull freeze frame, fuel trims and misfire data first
Pull it in and run a full workup
P0420 means converter — sell the converter

nodes.prompt: On the lift, scan tool connected. What's your move?

options.label: Graph both O2 sensors and force a mixture change
Smoke-test the exhaust ahead of the rear sensor
Check fuel trims and misfire counters
Check exhaust backpressure for a restricted converter
Clear the code and tell them to drive it a while
I'm ready to commit to a root cause

nodes.prompt: A healthy converter stores and releases oxygen. Compared with the upstream sensor, what should that make the downstream sensor do?
nodes.explanation: A working converter buffers the exhaust, so the rear sensor goes lazy and steady. A rear signal that mirrors the front means the converter isn't storing oxygen — or something is skewing that sensor.

options.label: Mirror the upstream sensor switch for switch
Switch noticeably faster than the upstream sensor does
Stay relatively steady instead of switching with it
Drop to a fixed zero volts once it is hot

nodes.prompt: You graph both O2 sensors at operating temperature and force the mixture rich, then lean, watching how each one responds.

options.label: Log it and smoke-test the exhaust as well
Log it and check trims and misfire data
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: Why can a pinhole exhaust leak ahead of the rear O2 sensor set a catalyst-efficiency code?
nodes.explanation: Negative pressure pulses draw outside air in through the leak. The rear sensor sees that oxygen and reports a converter that isn't storing any — a false P0420 on a good converter.

options.label: It drops backpressure enough to stall the converter
Pulses draw outside air in, so the rear sensor sees oxygen
It cools the converter below its light-off temperature
It makes the upstream sensor over-report the fuel trim

nodes.prompt: You block the tailpipe, fill the exhaust with smoke, and walk the system from the manifold back, looking for where it escapes.

options.label: Log it and graph the O2 sensors as well
Log it and check trims and misfire data
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: You pull freeze frame, watch short and long-term fuel trims at idle and cruise, and check misfire counters cylinder by cylinder under load.

options.label: Log it and graph the O2 sensors
Log it and smoke-test the exhaust
Log it and commit

nodes.prompt: You thread a gauge into the upstream O2 bung and check exhaust backpressure at idle and at a raised RPM.
nodes.continueLabel: Log it and get back to the workup

nodes.prompt: You clear the code and send it out to see whether it comes back.
nodes.continueLabel: That isn't a diagnosis — back to the workup

nodes.prompt: Commit to a specific root cause. The customer is deciding whether to spend $1,400 on your word.

options.label: It's an exhaust leak ahead of the rear sensor — repair the pipe
It's the downstream O2 sensor lying about a good converter — replace it
The converter is dead and a misfire killed it — fix both
The converter is dead — replace the converter
The other shop already said converter — just sell it
Clear it and tell them to keep driving

nodes.prompt: You replace the cracked flex pipe section and confirm the exhaust is sealed ahead of the rear sensor.
You replace the downstream O2 sensor with an OE-grade unit.
You install a new catalytic converter. (Book job: $1,400.)
You fix the cylinder-3 misfire — coil, plug and injector checked — and install a new converter behind it.
You clear the code and hand back the keys with a 'let us know if it comes back.'
Before this goes back to the customer — how do you prove the repair?

options.label: Run a drive cycle until the catalyst monitor completes
Light's out and it idles fine — release it

nodes.prompt: What actually proves a catalyst-code repair before the car leaves?
nodes.explanation: The catalyst monitor only runs under specific drive conditions. Until it completes and passes, nothing is proven — a light that is off may just mean the test hasn't run yet.

options.label: Drive it until the catalyst monitor completes and passes
Clear the code and confirm it stays off before they leave
Confirm the rear sensor reads a steady 0.45 volts at idle
Bring it to temperature and watch that the light stays off

nodes.prompt: You run the drive cycle, watching the catalyst monitor's readiness status and the rear sensor's behaviour the whole way.

The catalyst monitor runs and passes, the rear sensor behaves the way a good converter makes it behave, and the light stays off. If it was the converter, you sold it on evidence. If it wasn't, you saved the customer $1,400.
P0420 is back, and so is the customer. Whatever set it the first time is still on the car.
